parole.significato: Judas tree, a small, deciduous tree of the species Cercis siliquastrum
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ارغوان (erguvan), from Classical Persian اَرْغُوَان (arġuwān, “purple; Judas tree”), from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (ʾlgwkʾn' /⁠argawān⁠/, “purple”), ultimately from Akkadian 𒋠𒍝𒆳𒋛𒀀 (argawannu, “red purple”).

parole.significato: kesme, kind of homemade noodles or vermicelli prepared by laying long, thin strips of dough out to dry
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ارشته (erişte), from Classical Persian رِشْتَه (rišta), ultimately from Middle Persian 𐭥𐭱𐭲𐭢 (lštk' /⁠rištag⁠/). For the initial e- compare oruç (“fasting, abstinence”) and orospu (“whore, bitch, slut”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فهرست (fihrist), Classical Persian فِهْرِسْت (fihrist), from Middle Persian 𐭯𐭤𐭥𐭮𐭲 (phrst /⁠pahrist⁠/).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فیروزه (firuze), from earlier پیروزه (piruze, “turquoise”), from Classical Persian پیروزَه (pērōza), ultimately from Middle Persian *pērōzag (“turquoise”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كل (gül), from Classical Persian گُل (gul, “flower”), from Middle Persian gwl (gul, “rose, flower”), from Old Persian *vr̥dah, Proto-Iranian *wardah. Thus derives from the same etymon as English rose and Arabic وَرْد (ward).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كرز (gürz, “mace”), from Classical Persian گُرْز (gurz), from Middle Persian [Term?].

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish خانه (ḫāne), from Classical Persian خَانَه (xāna), from Middle Persian 𐭡𐭩𐭲𐭠 (xānag), from Old Persian *vahanam (“house”), from Proto-Iranian *wāhana (“habitation”), from Proto-Iranian *Hwah-, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hwas-, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂wes-.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish خنجر (hancer), borrowed from Classical Persian خَنْجَر (xanjar).

parole.significato: satisfied, pleased, content, contented, in a state of satisfaction
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish خشنود (hoşnud, “satisfied, pleased, content”), from Classical Persian خشنود (xušnūd, “content, satisfied”), from Middle Persian [script needed] (hwšnwt' /⁠hušnūd⁠/, “contented, happy”).

parole.significato: fig, the pear-shaped, edible fruit of the tree Ficus carica
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish انجیر (incir, “fig”), from Classical Persian انجیر (anjīr, “fig”), from Middle Persian ʾncyl (anjīr, “fig”).

parole.significato: amber, a yellow to brown fossil resin from extinct coniferous trees, used for jewellery or decoration
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كهربار (kehribar, kehrübar), vulgar form of كهربا (kehrüba), from Classical Persian کهربا (kahrubâ), from Middle Persian khlpʾd (kah-rubāy, “amber”).

parole.significato: celery, a cultivated plant of the species Apium graveolens, whose stalks are eaten as a vegetable
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كرویز (kereviz), from Classical Persian کرویز (karaviz), obsolete form of کرفس (karafs, “celery”), ultimately from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (karafs /⁠klps⁠/, “celery”).

parole.significato: coriander, any annual herb of the species Coriandrum sativum, used in many cuisines
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كشنش (kişniş, “coriander”), from Classical Persian گشنیز (gišniz, “coriander”), ultimately from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (gšnyc /⁠gišnīz⁠/, “coriander”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish كنجد (küncüd), from Classical Persian کنجد (kunjud, “sesame”), ultimately from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (kwncyt' /⁠kunjid⁠/, “sesame”).

parole.significato: marjoram, any herb of the species Origanum majorana, having aromatic leaves
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مرجانكوش (mercanköş), vulgarized form of Classical Persian مَرْزَنْگوش (marzangōš), ultimately from Middle Persian [script needed] (mlcngwš /⁠marzangōš⁠/, “marjoram”).

parole.significato: any kind of small, spherical object, such as a bead, especially one made of glass
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مهره (mühre, “bead; grinding shell; vertebra”), from Old Anatolian Turkish مهره (mühre), from Classical Persian مهره (muhra), ultimately from Middle Persian [script needed] (mwhlk' /⁠muhrag⁠/, “bead, vertebra, piece (in backgammon, etc.)”).

parole.significato: seal, a stamp used to impress a design on a soft substance
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish مهر (mühr, mühür), from Classical Persian مهر (muhr, “seal”), ultimately from Middle Persian 𐫖𐫇𐫍𐫡 (mwhr /⁠muhr⁠/, “seal”).

parole.significato: narcissus, daffodil, any of several bulbous flowering plants of the genus Narcissus
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish نركس (nergis), from Classical Persian نرگس (nargis), from Middle Persian nlgs (nargis), ultimately from Ancient Greek νάρκισσος (nárkissos).

parole.significato: chickpea, an annual plant of the species Cicer arietinum, cultivated for its edible seeds
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish نخود (nohud, “chickpea”), from Classical Persian نخود (naxōd, “chickpea”), from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (nhwt' /⁠naxōd⁠/, “chickpea”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پازار (pazar), بازار (bazar, “bazaar, marketplace; Sunday”), from Classical Persian بازار (bāzār, “market”), from Middle Persian [script needed] (wʾčʾl /⁠wāzār⁠/).

parole.significato: fasting observed by Christians and Jews on specific days, as opposed to the Islamic one
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پرهیز (perhiz, “abstinence; diet; fasting”), from Classical Persian پَرْهیزْ (parhēz, “abstinence, avoiding; diet, fasting”), from Middle Persian [script needed] (pʾhlyc /⁠pahrēz⁠/, “defence; care”).

parole.significato: prophet (one who speaks by divine inspiration)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پیغامبر (peyğamber, “prophet, messenger”), from Classical Persian پیغامبر (payġâmbar, “prophet, messenger”), from Middle Persian pgtʾmbl (payğāmbar, “messenger, apostle”).

parole.significato: term used to indicate messengers, guards, and later officials who participated in certain ceremonies in elaborate attire
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish پیك (peyk), from Classical Persian پیک (peyk, “messenger, courier”), from Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (pdk' /⁠payg⁠/, “foot-soldier, courier”).

parole.significato: cheese, a dairy product made from curdled milk

parole.significato: rhubarb, any plant of the genus Rheum, having large leaves and long, edible leafstalks
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish راوند (ravend, “rhubarb”), from Classical Persian ریوند (rivand, “rhubarb”), itself from Middle Persian *rēwand.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish رنك (renk), from Classical Persian رَنْگ (rang), Middle Persian lng (rang), from Proto-Iranian *ra(n)ǰ- (“to colour, dye”).

parole.significato: fennel, a flowering plant of the species Foeniculum vulgare and its bulb, eaten as a vegetable
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish رزنه (rezene), from Classical Persian رازیانه (râziyâne), ultimately from Middle Persian *rāziyānag.

parole.significato: jasmine, any of several flowering plants of the genus Jasminum, mostly native to Asia
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish یاسمین (yasemin), from Classical Persian یَاسَمِین (yāsamīn), a variant of یاسمن (yâsaman, “jasmine”), ultimately from Middle Persian 𐭩𐭠𐭮𐭬𐭭𐭠 (yʾsmn' /⁠yāsaman⁠/, “jasmine”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زندان (zindân), borrowed from Classical Persian زندان (zindān), from Middle Persian [script needed] (zyndʾn').
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چوبان (çoban), from Classical Persian چوپَان (čōpān), from Middle Persian 𐫢𐫇𐫁𐫀𐫗 (šwbʾn /⁠šubān⁠/), ultimately from Old Persian *fšupāna.

parole.significato: planetree, especially the oriental plane (Platanus orientalis)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چِنَار (çınâr), borrowed from Classical Persian چِنَار (činār), from Middle Persian cynʾl (/⁠činār⁠/).

parole.significato: buzzard, buteo, any of several birds of prey in the genus Buteo
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شاهین (şahin, “peregrine falcon”), from Classical Persian شاهین (šāhīn, “falcon”), ultimately from Middle Persian [script needed] (*šāhēn, literally “majestic, kingly”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شهر (şehir), from Classical Persian شَهْر (šahr).
